title: DAP note from F1: every section written + planted facts recalled
hypothesis: The DAP template produces a complete note that captures the session's key facts.

sections.title: Data
sections.html:
This was a 50-minute individual session utilizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) for a client presenting with Panic Disorder (F41.0).

The Client reported a rough week, noting a panic attack at the grocery store checkout line on Tuesday where their heart pounded, leading them to leave the cart and exit the store. The client reported thoughts of passing out in front of others and being perceived as crazy, rating the belief at 90% in the moment and 40% later at home. The client completed two out of three assigned thought records. Sleep was reported as poor, averaging four hours per night with early awakening around 3:00 AM. The client reported starting sertraline 50 mg approximately two weeks ago via their primary care provider, with initial mild nausea that has since resolved. Safety screening revealed no thoughts of self-harm or suicidality. During the session, the Therapist introduced interoceptive exposure; the client spun in a chair for 30 seconds to induce dizziness, reporting anxiety that peaked at 6 and decreased to 3 within two minutes. The client mentioned unhelpful feedback from their sister, Dana, and declined an invitation to bring her to a future session at this time.

sections.title: Assessment
sections.html: The client demonstrates partial engagement with CBT homework, completing two thought records and showing awareness of cognitive shifts when rating the belief in passing out from 90% down to 40% retrospectively. The interoceptive exposure exercise was successfully tolerated, providing in-session experiential learning that physical sensations peak and subside without catastrophic outcomes or avoidance. Sleep disturbance persists at four hours per night. The client denies suicidal ideation or intent to self-harm. Progress toward goals includes developing insight into panic symptoms and distress tolerance, though avoidance behaviors in public spaces remain a target for intervention.

sections.title: Plan
sections.html:
• Complete thought records three times before the next session.
  • Practice the spinning interoceptive exposure exercise once a day at home.
  • Conduct an in-vivo exposure task by returning to the grocery store on a quiet Saturday morning and staying until anxiety decreases by half.
  • Continue individual CBT sessions weekly.
